newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU fuel prices down versus income in 1980-94.
newsitem.headline: EU fuel prices down versus income in 1980-94.

text.p: Fuel prices in relation to income has fallen sharply in 10 European Union countries between 1980 and 1994, according to a report published on Monday by the EU's statistical office, Eurostat.
"As the price of fuel relative to disposable income has fallen, the consumption of fuels has increased," Eurostat said.
It used a measure for the fuel price related to the average disposable income (percentage of per capita net disposable income required to buy 1,000 litres of a weighted mix of fuel).
It said relative prices on average in the 10 countries in the survey fell from 7.7 in 1980 to 4.9 in 1994.
Among big consumers, it declined to 4.0 from 7.3 in Germany, to 5.1 from 8.2 in Britain and to 4.1 from 6.8 in France.

The same report said transport's share of total final energy consumption in the EU rose to 30.8 percent in 1994 from 16.7 percent in 1960. "It has now overtaken that of industry," the Eurostat statement said.

The report, worked out together with the European Commission's directorate-general for the environment, said fuel combustion was the main problem for emissions of carbon dioxide, which have continued to increase.

"Public transport is the most energy efficient form of passenger transport, and a shift towards it from personal car usage would result in lower emissions and slower depletion of fossil fuel stocks," it said.
